source.title: CoE: Chain-of-Explanation via Automatic Visual Concept Circuit Description and Polysemanticity Quantification
source.authors: Wen-Long Yu; Qi-Long Wang; Chuang Liu; Dong Li; Qing-Hua Hu

record.tranche_reason: The study measures visual-channel polysemanticity with concept atoms and Concept Polysemanticity Entropy (CPE), rather than counting neuron poles by main job. Its comparisons across visual models, layers, and XAI methods also bear on the architecture-and-tools version.
record.gate_note: The study reports CPE measurements, concept-atom counts, and comparisons of CPE across layers, models, and XAI methods. Its local-explanation quality scores and example predictions do not measure neuron polysemanticity or the architecture/tool trends in the claim, so they are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures an entropy score (CPE) over GPT-4o word descriptions of the top 15 image patches per channel in ResNet and CLIP vision models. It does not count the share of neurons or poles with one main job, and it studies no language models. V1 and V2 concern language models, so the rows cannot bear on them. V3, V5, V6 and V7 are not addressed. For V4, CPE is a different construct from the share of interpretable neurons, and it has a floor well above zero: a channel described as 'lobster, red, claws' on all 15 patches still scores 0.70 (Table S8). Its comparison across XAI methods shows that this proxy depends on the method. It does not show whether better tools or modern architectures raise the share of neurons that are interpretable. These findings belong under fits_no_version, not verdicts.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct, with two corrections. First, the rise with ResNet depth holds only for the relevance-based CRP method and reverses with activation-based extraction; the authors take this to show the XAI method choice is critical. Second, the authors report 75% agreement between CPE and human pairwise judgments, and a 36% average gain in explanation scores for CoE.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses vision-model concept extraction, prompted language-model descriptions, semantic clustering, and entropy over concept-atom frequencies. It does not use the Qwen3-32B pole-audit method or held-out activation tests described in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: CPE trends vary with layer, model depth, architecture, and XAI method. The authors also attribute CLIP results in part to the ImageNet validation set being out-of-distribution for CLIP.

fits_no_version.finding: ResNet152 channels average 12.7 to 18.3 clustered description atoms per channel; intro reports about 13 on average. CPE ranges 0.5–1, and most channels show noticeable polysemanticity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Vision CNN channels, described by an LVLM from their top patches, carry many distinct description atoms (high description entropy).

fits_no_version.finding: Averaged CPE peaks at Stage 3 and is lower in Stages 1 and 4. Under CRP it rises slightly with ResNet depth; under activation-based extraction it falls; MILAN concepts score lower.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Measured polysemanticity of vision channels depends on layer and on the concept-extraction method, with depth trends reversing across methods.

fits_no_version.finding: CLIP-ResNet50 channels show higher CPE than ImageNet ResNet50; the authors attribute this partly to out-of-distribution probe data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The polysemanticity proxy is higher in CLIP vision channels when they are probed with ImageNet-val.

record.problems: The study's semantic atoms are generated from a fixed set of 15 image patches using prompted LVLM outputs and 13 semantic directions; the text reports no held-out-activation validation of those descriptions. CPE is a proxy rather than a direct count of poles by number of jobs. The reported results provide no statistical uncertainty estimates, and some comparisons are reported as qualitative trends without exact values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Local-explanation score tables and prediction examples were omitted because they assess explanation quality, not neuron polysemanticity or the architecture/tool claims. Exact plotted values not stated in accompanying text were not transcribed.

untested.parts: No Qwen3-32B or any language model; no share of poles with one or two jobs, or not understood.
No language models, MoE models, or scaling to trillions of parameters.
No InceptionV1 cat/car neuron, no pose analysis, no recursive generalization.
No measure of the share of interpretable neurons. Architecture/regularization effects and the 5%-to-99% estimates are not tested; CPE comparisons only show that the proxy depends on the method.
Concept circuits are used for explanations, but there is no test of neuron-based attribution graphs against replacement models.
No held-out prediction of where channels fire.

record.verdict_notes: This is a borderline case for V4, since the paper compares XAI tools and architectures, but CPE is not an interpretable-neuron share. CPE has a high floor from padding: the near-monosemantic lobster channel scores 0.70 and the shark channel 0.81. CPE also inflates atom counts because the prompt forces 3 words per patch, so it cannot separate 'one main job' from polysemanticity. The measure's validity rests only on 75% pairwise agreement with humans. CoE explanation-score tables measure the authors' own method and were rightly excluded as rows.

versions.untested_parts: Does not audit Qwen3-32B or language-model neuron poles, calculate the claimed percentages of poles with one or two jobs or not understood, or test explanations on held-out activations.
No language models, mixture-of-experts models, or trillion-parameter models are evaluated.
Does not analyze InceptionV1 cat-and-car neurons, pose, or recursive generalization.
Does not test InceptionV1-sized vision models or the 5%-to-99% estimates, regularization, or whether architecture or tool improvements causally increase the share of interpretable neurons.
Does not test attribution graphs built from a large language model's own neurons or compare them with a trained replacement model.
Does not test explanations on activations withheld from their construction or measure where a neuron fires on new examples.
Does not score language-model neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

rows.subject: ResNet152
rows.operation_detail: Counted distinct concept atoms per concept after semantic clustering.
rows.measure: Average number of non-overlapping semantic atoms per concept
rows.note: The paper reports an average atom count, not a proportion of poles with a particular number of jobs.
rows.check: Vision-model channels, not Qwen3-32B neuron poles. The count of 18.3 clustered atoms includes per-image filler words that the prompt forces (3 words per patch), so it is not a count of jobs.

rows.subject: ResNet152
rows.operation_detail: Counted distinct concept atoms per concept after semantic clustering.
rows.measure: Average number of non-overlapping semantic atoms per concept
rows.note: The paper reports an average atom count, not a proportion of poles with a particular number of jobs.
rows.check: Same issue as R1: an atom count from forced 3-word descriptions of patches, measured on vision channels, not language-model poles.

rows.subject: ResNet152
rows.measure: CPE range and qualitative distribution across concepts
rows.value: CPE ranges from a maximum of 1 to a minimum of 0.5; most concepts demonstrate a noticeable level of polysemanticity.
rows.note: CPE is the study's entropy-based proxy for polysemanticity; it is not a direct count of the share of poles with one main job.
rows.check: The CPE range is a proxy on vision channels. Because of padding, the floor is high; a uniform lobster channel scores 0.70. It cannot show a share with one main job.

rows.subject: ResNet152
rows.operation_detail: Calculated CPE for two example concepts extracted by different XAI methods.
rows.note: An illustrative channel-level example; the study does not state that it is representative of all channels.
rows.check: This is an illustrative single channel: concept 75, Layer 4, CRP. It is mostly shark/blue/water, which would plausibly count as one main job, yet it scores CPE 0.81.

rows.subject: ResNet152
rows.operation_detail: Calculated CPE for two example concepts extracted by different XAI methods.
rows.note: An illustrative channel-level example; the study does not state that it is representative of all channels.
rows.check: Illustrative single channel (concept 697, Layer 4, MILAN). It is a vision model, not V1's subject.

rows.subject: ResNet152
rows.operation_detail: Compared averaged CPE across four key layers.
rows.value: The averaged CPE peaks in Stage 3; the shallowest and deepest layers have lower values.
rows.note: The authors say the layer pattern indicates less polysemanticity for elementary and abstract concepts and more ambiguity in intermediate layers. Exact plotted values are not stated in the text.
rows.check: A layer profile of the CPE proxy; it does not measure the share of interpretable neurons as a function of tools or architecture. The plotted values span only about 0.82–0.87.

rows.subject: ResNet50, ResNet101, and ResNet152
rows.operation_detail: Compared averaged CPE across models of different depths.
rows.value: CPE shows a rising trend as the number of layers increases.
rows.note: The authors interpret this as a direct proportional relationship between model complexity and polysemanticity. Exact plotted values are not stated in the text.
rows.check: A depth trend of CPE under CRP, with values roughly 0.842–0.847, a tiny spread. It is not an interpretable-share measure, and model depth is not V4's architecture or regularization contrast.

rows.subject: ResNet50, ResNet101, and ResNet152
rows.operation_detail: Compared CPE results across XAI methods and model depths.
rows.value: The polysemanticity observed with the activation-based method diminishes as model complexity increases.
rows.note: The paper reports a trend across model depths, not exact per-model values.
rows.check: A depth trend of the proxy under the activation-based method. It shows that the metric depends on the method, not that the interpretable share rises with better tools.

rows.subject: ResNet50, ResNet101, and ResNet152
rows.operation_detail: Compared CPE results across XAI methods and model depths.
rows.value: The relevance-based method exhibits the contrasting trend: CPE rises with model complexity.
rows.note: The paper reports a trend across model depths, not exact per-model values.
rows.check: This row duplicates R7, the relevance-based depth trend. It is a proxy measure.

rows.subject: ResNet152
rows.operation_detail: Compared CPE for concepts extracted by different XAI methods.
rows.measure: CPE relative to other XAI methods
rows.baseline: Other XAI methods; exact reference values not stated
rows.value: Concepts derived from maximum mutual information exhibit lower CPE values.
rows.note: The authors qualify this comparison because the method relies on manually annotated concepts and lacks automation and flexibility.
rows.check: MILAN concepts score lower CPE, but they come from manual annotation. This is a difference in the measurement pipeline, not an interpretable share.

rows.subject: CLIP-ResNet50
rows.operation_detail: Compared averaged CPE across model architectures and layers.
rows.value: The CLIP vision branch exhibits greater polysemanticity; its CPE is lowest in Stage 4 and peaks in intermediate stages, with high polysemanticity in the shallowest stage.
rows.note: The authors suggest the result may reflect the ImageNet validation data being out-of-distribution for CLIP and the use of 15 patches per concept.
rows.check: The CLIP-RN50 vs ResNet50 difference is confounded: the authors attribute it partly to ImageNet-val being out of distribution for CLIP. The measure is a proxy.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: ResNet152 visual concept channels in the reported ImageNet-validation experiments
reader_labels.reason: The reported atom counts and CPE results indicate substantial polysemanticity in these visual channels, inconsistent with a simple picture of nearly all units having one job; however, they do not directly establish the share of poles with one, two, or unknown jobs. Rows R1–R5.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Layers, model depths, architectures, and XAI methods tested in the vision-model experiments
reader_labels.reason: CPE varies by layer and architecture, and its trend with model depth differs between activation-based and relevance-based methods, so the result depends on both the measurement tool and setting. Rows R6–R11.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Relevance-based CPE across ResNet50, ResNet101, and ResNet152
reader_labels.reason: For the relevance-based method, the reported CPE rises with model depth, contrary to a simple claim that greater model complexity makes concepts more interpretable. Row R7.
